newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close mixed, Corimon dominates.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close mixed, Corimon dominates.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed mixed in a session dominated by trade in Corimon and worries over the government's privatisation program, traders said.
"The market's being held back by fears over the legal requirements needed to back the CANTV sale," said Merinvest broker Boris Molina.
The bolsa's index closed up a slight 0.20 percent as 18 shares rose, 15 fell and nine closed flat.
Investors will be watching for the outcome of Wednesday's discussion of the Privatisation Reform Bill that paves the way for the CANTV share offering, Molina said.
The bill was postponed today after students protesting tough economic reforms blocked the streets around Congress.
A total of 32 million shares traded worth 3 billion bolivars ($6.4 million), according to exchange figures.
Trade in newly released Corimon B shares accounted for over half that total.

The price fell 3.75 bolivars from its opening to close at 12.75. Company creditors, forced to securitise debts into B shares as part of the company's financial restructuring, were offloading their shares for cash, traders said.
"The stock price is very unstable at the moment," said one.
Among the day's other major trades, Electricidad de Caracas gained 0.25 bolivar to end at 540.25, while steel company Sivensa lost 2.00 bolivars to end at 350.00.
